data_identity.comparison: Exact values, shapes and dtypes of every data.npz array.

final_training_audit.note: Initial backbone hashes are compared across available same-seed arms; energy hashes/grid across GF arms. Data-dependent GF residual normalization and selected checkpoint step may differ.

metric.units_in_json: Fractions; multiply by 100 for percent or paired percentage points.
metric.time_aggregation: Arithmetic mean of per-time pooled error over every saved time in the specified interval.
metric.observed_window: [0,1.25] includes all saved times, not only six supervised frames.

gf_without_ssv.sign: Treatment minus baseline; negative is lower error after adding the component.

gf_with_ssv.sign: Treatment minus baseline; negative is lower error after adding the component.

ssv_without_gf.sign: Treatment minus baseline; negative is lower error after adding the component.

ssv_with_gf.sign: Treatment minus baseline; negative is lower error after adding the component.

protocol_notes: All four arms use exactly the same ordinary two-Gaussian initial conditions, splits, spatial grid and six labels through t=1.25.
Shared SSV uses the source-selected gamma, frozen with alpha=beta=0.5. Removing GF does not trigger another gamma selection.
Physical-coordinate arms have alpha=beta=0. All arms share the backbone scale and matched same-seed initial weights.
The existing source SSV+GF fits are reused; the other three arms are separately fitted from fresh initial weights.
Every main-table statistic, paired contrast and curve uses the four-way completed seed intersection; completion counts are listed separately.
This is a new six-frame experiment with a gamma selector, not a reproduction of the original paper's three-frame Gaussian experiment.
Only saved predictions are analyzed. No additional network training or inference is performed by this report.

prespecified_example.selection: test_001 and optimizer seed 0 are fixed in advance; no error-based selection.

frozen_latent.interpretation: Prediction counterfactual with the same trained weights, not an independently trained no-latent or no-GF ablation. It measures the effect of continuing learned latent evolution beyond the observed endpoint in these checkpoints.
